patch_description: Replace the single-sample greedy with a beam search: maintain multiple partial schedules (beam width k), expand each beam by all remaining transactions, keep the k best by incremental makespan cost. This explores the ordering space far more broadly than the current sampled greedy, which only ever considers one random candidate per step and often locks in bad early choices. Beam search with full expansion avoids sampling noise and keeps multiple promising orderings alive, yielding much lower makespans. To keep it tractable, use a lookahead-limited expansion and randomized restarts to escape local optima.
